text: I purchased two vent covers for my Class A motorhome only to realize that the Fantastic Fan Vent had different dimensions.  So I purchased this Dometic Fan Tastic Fan vent and it worked perfectly!  I watched several installation videos on Youtube to check for any "gotchas" and these videos absolutely helped with installation procedures and hints.
You can leave the vent open when traveling and when it rains.
The white Fantastic Fan vent cover is of very nice quality and easy to install . My son was very pleased with this addition to his van .

Before ordering this product, I called Dometic directly. After 37 minutes on hold, I was told "The fit is not right for that model Dometic fan" (DFV4100). I then asked "What model WILL fit it"? "There are problems associated with that model, so we do not have one available that will work". No apologies, no suggestions. Just a very matter matter-of-fact answer.
Customer service at it's worst.

All in all, kind of a little disappointed. Time will tell how long it will hold up.

This vent hood is about one and one half inches taller that our previous MaxxAir hood. This means that the cover of our Fantastic Fan will now open fully for better air flow. It’s also translucent white not heavy smoke tint so more light comes through. The mounting system is the typical four clamps screwed into the roof, two on each side.

Sadly, for a hood that is this expensive, there is NO BUG SCREEN INCLUDED. There is a grill styled opening, but no bug screen. Our original MaxxAir hood included a bug screen. (No, the old screen was not “adaptable”!) The easiest and least expensive solution is installing some fiberglass bug screen material on the inside of the grate using the same tube of roof caulk you will need to caulk over the mounting screws. Caution: be sure to use caulk designed for your roof material. Cut the material to fit inside with a one inch overlap on each side. I used a 10” by 19” sized piece. Lay a bead of caulk along the inside edge of the grate and press the screen material into the caulk bead. See the attached photo. Save a little in the tube of caulk for your mounting screws piece of the install.

I installed this on a 2021 Airstream Flying Cloud over my Fan-tastic vent fan.  Install took me about 15 minutes (just make sure when you get on the roof you take everything with you so you aren't up-down-up-down). I will be buying a second one for the rear fan.  They are a little more expensive than other vent covers, and I cannot attest to how they hold up long term, but for me the fit and installation were great.

When our Whirlpool washing machine went on the fritz, I thought for sure it was going to cost me a lot of money.  Thanks to a quick Internet search and a helpful YouTube video, I purchased this motor coupling and installed it myself in about 45 minutes.  If I had more room to maneuver in the wash room, I probably could've finished the installation quicker.  Not being mechanically inclined, I was surprised at how easy it was to repair the machine.  If you determine this is the part that failed on your washing machine, I suggest spending the twelve bucks on the part and installing it yourself.  I'm sure I saved at least a hundred bucks over having an appliance repair guy come out to fix it.

I was a little cautious about ordering this part due to all the comments about how difficult the new metal sleeved units are to install. I am happy to report that it isn't. Yes it is a tighter fit than the original all-plastic part, but it isn't rocket science. Place a small socket or extension on the metal sleeve as a drift and TAP it onto the motor and transmission shafts with a mallet or hammer. You won't damage the part unless you are careless and strike it on the plastic. It took me less than 2 minutes to install with the motor and transmission on the bench.

The design and construction of this coupling far exceeds the original it replaced.  The rubber piece is solid as opposed to being hollow.  In addition the couplings have a metal insert which mounts to the motor.  Furthermore, the price was about $10 cheaper than the local appliance shop.

Bought this part based on a Youtube diagnosis of the sound my washer was making. Thank goodness the old part was actually broken. Looks sturdier than the part it replaced. Ten minutes to install, still working very well.

My Kenmore washing machines motor coupling stripped the splines and I needed to replace it. The one I had did not look like the one shown as the replacement but the info indicated it would fit. The price was right so I ordered it. It was delivered sooner than the scheduled date. It only took about an hour to remove the old part and install the new one and it worked great!
Exactly as described.  Relatively easy to install (weight of assembly could be a challenge for some people).  Recommend replacing brake and lining when you do this part.

Note that the main picture is not accurate. This coupling has a METAL center rather than plastic/nylon center.

Many websites recommend that you use a coupling with a plastic/nylon center. If you use the metal one, you run the risk of the metal from the coupling stripping the post of your motor. It is much better to keep the post of your motor in tact, and let the plastic/nylon center of this coupling take the wear and tear.

I purchased two of these couplings so that I would have a spare. The first one failed during the second batch of wash. The second one and the replacement coupling sent when I notified the vendor all failed in about the same time. In all cases the metal hub came loose from the plastic sprocket. To make sure there wasn't something wrong with my washing machine causing the failures I purchased the all plastic coupling without the metal hub. It has been working well ever since. I spent a lot of time replacing couplings. Don't buy this coupling. Buy the one without the metal hub.

This is normal since the part is getting acclimated to the machine.  Have had it on for about a month now, roughly 25 loads of wash, still going strong!  15 bucks spent saved me $500 on a new machine.  BTW:  if you're worried you can put this part on, don't be!  It literally took me 35 minutes with the help of the MANY Youtube videos out there.  It is a really easy fix if you are even remotely handy (as in, you know how a screw driver works).  Definitely worth at least trying before buying a machine.

Thanks to a YouTube video, I was able to diagnose the problem and buy the right part.  The part arrived well within the indicated time, and I was able to install it and get the machine back up and running.  The extra metal bushing makes it more robust than the original.  Very pleased.

I am concerned about the "improved" metal bushings on this part. I had a hard time getting the old all plastic coupling off of the transmission. Unlike some of the other models. my machine (an older Kitchenaid) had very little access to the sides and back of the old coupler - there is no way in my machine to get behind it with a screwdriver or hammer claw because the coupler is mostly surrounded by the cast iron housing of the transmission.  Even removing the faceplate of the transmission would not have helped.  Finally I hit upon the idea of slipping a piece of string behind the coupler and pulling it off the shaft - this worked great for the old all plastic part. But in order to get the new part down flush with the end of the shaft I had to (as the online videos suggest) drive it down by tapping it with the back of a screwdriver being hit by a hammer.  So now it is on the shaft very snug metal on metal.  I hope it doesn't break again because I have no idea how I could ever pull this off the shaft again - I doubt the string trick will work for something that was driven on with a hammer.  Ironically the old part in my machine failed by breaking off the prongs (all but 1) and not at the center.  It would have actually made it easier to remove from the shaft if the old part had failed at the center hole but in fact the connection to the shaft remained perfectly intact , so the bushing was not a failure point (in my machine) to begin with.
